description.narrative: Ind. 1.1.1.: % of targeted youth (men and women) involved in developing the innovative platforms and use it to document breaches of HR, report on them and tell stories about life in EJ compared to the baseline values

comment.narrative: Youth were 100 involved in developing the platforms. The platforms are led by young content makers who promote productions on the platforms related to breaches of HR and stories about life in EJ. By enabling the youth to do so the social and political space for youth in EJ has improved. Yplus produced 357 multimedia productions humanbased stories social cards photo essays REEL videos infographics. These were published on Facebook Instagram Twitter YouTube and on Yplus website. Jerusalem24 radio station on the other hand broadcasted live on air published programs and news related to the situation in EJ over 10000 productions published on their social media platforms and website. Their productions included news segments mainly in English but also in Hebrew. The action gave the opportunity to the youths to be involved in developing content related to the IHL and IHRL breaches and the daily life in EJ. First a total of 57 targeted youth aged between 1630 years old voiced their stories in relation to breaches of IHL and IHRL through Yplus productions. Second a total 90 youth took part of an intensive internship program and were provided with the tools experience and knowledge needed to enable them to produce creative content write film or direct videos.The 90 interns constitute a new significant bulk or group of human resources in line with the plan to increase the baseline figure 8.5 . A vast majority of them have acquired both new skills motivation and ambitions to produce and publish blogs videos and other forms of media content on web pages and social media as witnessed by Yplus through their continued contacts with more than half of the interns after their internships. The utilization of a WhatsApp group has facilitated the exchange of information regarding relevant opportunities and events. It also serves as a platform for sharing links to blogs social media posts and websites where the interns stories and content are published. This communication channel enables Yplus to monitor and track the interns progress and engagement. For Jerusalem24 the primary means of engaging with young people in EJ is through the content it publishes on its website and social media platforms. As a relatively new media outlet having started broadcasting in May 2021 Jerusalem24 presents a fresh avenue of opportunities for young Jerusalemites to participate by sharing and commenting on stories. During the period between 2020 and 2023 Yplus recruited in total 90 young interns each one working six months with the specific aim to increase the number of youths to produce and publish stories about HR violations and life in EJ.It does not make sense to compare their experience with those who were randomly selected at the baseline. The evaluation team opted for qualitative methods such as focus group discussions to gather comprehensive and contextualized data for a more thorough assessment of the projects impact. Therefore the focus of the evaluation was on examining the impact of the internship program and the experiences of the interns rather than conducting a replication of the previous survey. In this case the evaluation team organized a focus group session with around 15 members of the media lab to reflect and discuss their experiences. The evaluation report says the following Outcome 1 has been achieved with good margins as the two outputs results were accomplished and through a good progress of the numeric indicators. On the one hand new media platforms were established and used and on the other young Jerusalemites gained capacity to publish stories and denounce violations of human rights. They constitute a resource base for national and international organisations companies and authorities.

The level of engagement of Palestinian DBs targeted through the action has increased. Six accountability sessions were implemented addressing areas of relevance to the reality of the Jerusalemites in EJ and the issues they suffer and challenge their existence in the city. The sessions focused on areas such as education economy culture labour and governance. In total six duty bearers participated in these sessions. There was also attendance representing different stakeholders. such as members from local NGOs university students work seekers and so on the sessions attendance reached 115 individuals. The sessions featured the Prime Minister Advisor of Arab and Islamic Funds Minister Dr. Nasser Qatami Deputy to the Palestinian Governor of East Jerusalem Mr. Abdallah Siam Head of Directorate of Education in Jerusalem Mr. Sameer Jebril Deputy Minister of Labour Samer Salameh Mr. Motasem Abu Gharbieh from the Higher Council of Sports and Youth and Mr. Nidal Melhem from the Palestine Monetary Authority. These accountability sessions including the follow up actions done by the project team afterwards with the attendees have remarkable actions taken by the official entities. For example the Higher Council of Youth and Sports reported working on sponsoring more activities in the Jerusalem governorate focusing on youth initiatives and are working on having more youth staff by creating 4 job opportunities for youth. The Palestinian Monetary Fund has agreed to be involved in the awareness raising campaign Bhimitkom which aim to increase the awareness of rights of youth with disabilities to access banking institutions and of the complaints system available to them in case they are denied access. Upon the completion of this action the assessment of the team is that the approach in this action of holding the Palestinian Authority accountable to its responsibilities in EJ by facilitating meetings with EJ youth is not perceived as particularly relevant. Considering the political situation in EJ the inability of the PA institutions to do meaningful efforts and the absence of parliamentary elections across oPt since 2006 such meetings have proven to be difficult to organize or manage as neither decision makers nor the youth have incentives to be in such meetings. On the other hand based on the final evaluation report the accountability sessions conducted by youth were deemed successful in fostering greater interaction between rights holders and Palestinian duty bearers DBs. These sessions served as a forum for discussing a range of topics including the right to education sports and economic matters in East Jerusalem.

Six accountability sessions were implemented addressing areas of relevance to the reality of the Jerusalemites in EJ and the issues they suffer and challenge their existence in the city. The sessions focused on areas such as education economy culture labour and governance. In total six duty bearers participated in these sessions. There was also attendance representing different stakeholders. such as members from local NGOs university students work seekers and so on the sessions attendance reached 115 individuals. The sessions featured the Prime Minister Advisor of Arab and Islamic Funds Minister Dr. Nasser Qatami Deputy to the Palestinian Governor of East Jerusalem Mr. Abdallah Siam Head of Directorate of Education in Jerusalem Mr. Sameer Jebril Deputy Minister of Labour Samer Salameh Mr. Motasem Abu Gharbieh from the Higher Council of Sports and Youth and Mr. Nidal Melhem from the Palestine Monetary Authority. These accountability sessions including the follow up actions done by the project team afterwards with the attendees have remarkable actions taken by the official entities. For example the Higher Council of Youth and Sports reported working on sponsoring more activities in the Jerusalem governorate focusing on youth initiatives and are working on having more youth staff by creating 4 job opportunities for youth. The Palestinian Monetary Fund has agreed to be involved in the awareness raising campaign Bhimitkom which aim to increase the awareness of rights of youth with disabilities to access banking institutions and of the complaints system available to them in case they are denied access. Upon the completion of this action the assessment of the team is that the approach in this action of holding the Palestinian Authority accountable to its responsibilities in EJ by facilitating meetings with EJ youth is not perceived as particularly relevant. The level of actions taken by the community members to preserve and promote communitybased tourism increased by 100. Communitybased tourism has been promoted expanded tested and implemented involving many target groups and beneficiaries including at the international level. The planned result was fully achieved. Capacity building programs were completed and facilities were developed like trails homestays tours and Women Centers laying a strong foundation for communitybased tourism to become a source of income for targeted communities. The targeted community members subjected to the capacity building trainings have asserted that they have gained valuable knowledge and skills related to communitybased tourism including practical application of theoretical knowledge related to managing trails and homestays and important issues like food processing and preserving gender issues as well as marketing their villages. The activities expanded capacities and knowledge of the local communities to first mobilize more community members and to invest in the cultural traditional and religious resources that were not sufficiently used before the action such as the Qbeiba Church as one of the most important religious and historical heritage in the occupied territories. From another point of view as a result of the action local councils started adopting initiatives to clean and reserve archaeological sites such as Khans. The restoration of the Khan and the nearby area included efforts by the council of Beit Duqqu local council and Ministry of Tourism Antiquities without external funds. The biking and hiking tracks also promote communitybased tourism in targeted communities and encourage visitors to come and encourage more community members to support CBT. These tracks will be utilised by the local community to continue promoting the communitybased tourism leading to preserve Palestinian culture. The delays caused due to the COVID19 pandemic and the related safety measures delaying the establishment and rehabilitation of different products like homestays women centres as well as capacity building programs hindered the ability to fully test the presumed assumptions. The assessment of the potential for receiving the local and international visitors at a larger scale has been difficult. As per the external evaluation the target is clearly achieved. The action has conducted a significant number of activities with a clear purpose to achieve this indicator. The large number of events and participants their focus and relevance are key aspects for the evaluation of how the indicators were monitored and progressed to reach the final target and contributing to the level of indicator.

At least one initiative was proposed to mitigate every risk identified by the PGs in all five communities. These initiatives included shortterm within Actions timeline and longterm initiatives outside Actions timeline low budget within Actions budget and high budget outside Actions budget initiatives as well as a number of responsible bodies including local Village CouncilsVCs community members and government bodies. An example of lowbudgetshortterm initiatives is the rehabilitation of the educational centre in Qbeiba an initiative that responds to social and educational risks within the community. An example of a longterm initiative is the development of a waste management system in Beit Sourik.Some initiatives required coordination. For example first aid training was conducted by the Ministry of Health MoH in all targeted communities. Civil Defence training was completed by the Civil Defence in Biddou Beit Anan and Qbeiba. These trainings increased local community knowledge about mitigating risks and also created a communication channel between MoH Civil Defence and PGs.

comment.narrative: Best practices are categorized as follows 1 networking and exchange among local communities 2 leveraging funds and enhancing the capacities of PGs for community benefit and 3 networking and coordination with external stakeholders. Progress towards this indicator has been visible throughout the Action. Community members participated in nine networking and exchange visits where seven were conducted within the Action two outside the Action. These visits provided a space for PG members to share their experiences and best practices with PGs from different communities. Furthermore PGs shared their feedback on the Community Led Action approach of implementation their increased involvement within the local community and how to improve their activities throughout the Action.Coordination with external stakeholders has developed substantially by the end of the Action. PG members started coordination with ministries suppliers and other organizations to further help mitigate the risks they face within their communities. For example Beit Duqqu PG coordinated with the Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities and were able to secure funding to renovate a historical building next to Ein Salman. Along with the initiative implemented by EJYMCA both initiatives will boost tourism to Ein Salman and preserve the Palestinian characteristic of it.The continuation and coordination for initiatives outside the Action activities was also highlighted. The PG in Beit Anan shared how they coordinated a campaign for women that needed support obtaining their driving licenses at a minimal charge. The campaign included providing training sessions for the theoretical test covering the cost of the theoretical test and covering the cost of the practical test if they passed on the first attempt. This initiative was funded by community members of Beit Anan residing abroad. A total of 87 women registered for the campaign and undertook the theoretical training approximately 75 women passed the theoretical test and approximately 50 women obtained their driving licenses.

comment.narrative: The project achieved its desired impact at a high level due to the establishment of new and strategic media outlets Yplus and Jerusalem24. The first has created a successful empowerment of youth subproject and the latter began an innovative journey that may lead to a sustainable radio in English and Hebrew. Young people in the city were supported to promote enhanced understanding nationally and internationally on their life in EJ and the action collaborated with them towards generating actions by different decision makers that addresses IHL and IHRL violations. The project has facilitated policy changes among decision makers while simultaneously preserving the Palestinian identity thereby enhancing the potential for a twostate solution with increased actions and participation from various stakeholders. Through the actions advocacy components changes in the political attitudes and behaviour towards the IsraelPalestinian conflict in two specific examples in Poland and Czech Republic were achieved. Here centre rightwing political parties positions have shifted as a result of the action. Through the action the level of engagement of Palestinian youth in EJ in promoting an understanding of the situation in EJ has clearly increased. In the baseline study and midterm review conducted in the first and second reporting period respectively findings showed that youth in EJ were clearly missing the adequate knowledge concerning the social economic cultural life and heritage in their city.
